title: What is haram?
description: What does haram mean in food? Understand prohibited sources, ingredient labels and why an unknown origin is a doubt rather than a verdict.
lead: Haram means prohibited under Islamic law. In food, it refers to ingredients or conditions that do not meet the applicable Islamic dietary requirements.
food_text: Pork and its derivatives, blood and alcoholic drinks are among the prohibited sources listed by Codex. A label can declare a prohibited source explicitly; a generic ingredient name may leave its origin or process unresolved.
criteria_text: BOTIA marks a label as Haram when it explicitly declares a prohibited ingredient, such as pork derivatives, alcohol or blood.
uncertainty_text: When the label does not establish the origin or process, BOTIA uses Mashbooh (doubt). Missing information is not proof that an ingredient is Halal or Haram.
limits_title: What BOTIA can and cannot conclude
can1: Detect prohibited ingredients when they are explicitly declared on the label.
can2: Distinguish a clear Haram trigger from an ingredient whose origin is merely uncertain.
can3: Show which declared ingredient caused the Haram result.
cannot1: Infer a Haram ingredient that is not declared on the label.
cannot2: Determine undeclared manufacturing processes or cross-contamination.
cannot3: Resolve cases where origin or processing is unknown; those remain Mashbooh rather than Haram.
